reply.thought: Before paying, I need to verify Alpha's refund work. I'll start by listing the orders and refunds to cross-check the handoff.
The refunds list matches Alpha's handoff exactly. Next I'll list the orders so I can check each refund against its order amount before paying anyone.

The refunds match Alpha's handoff, and each refund is below its order amount (211: 24506 of 38685, 213: 15133 of 31611, 214: 6668 of 35281), so nothing looks wrong. I'll get the net balance for the first customer, acme, rather than doing the arithmetic myself.
Acme's net balance of 48125 checks out: orders 210 and 213 total 63258, less the 213 refund of 15133. Refunds match the handoff and no order is over-refunded, so I'll continue with birch.
Birch's net of 42792 matches my check: orders 211 and 214 total 73966, less refunds of 24506 and 6668. Cobalt has no refunds on the ledger, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net of 46961 matches its orders 212 and 215 (32516 + 14445) with no refunds, and all three balances check out against the orders and refunds. Alpha's refund work is consistent, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme at 48125.
Acme's payout of 48125 was recorded. Birch's net of 42792 matches orders 211 and 214 (73966) less refunds 24506 and 6668, so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout of 42792 was recorded. The last customer is cobalt, with net 46961, which matches orders 212 and 215 (32516 + 14445) and has no refunds, so I'll record that payout.

All three payouts were recorded successfully. Each net balance matches the orders minus refunds: acme 63258 - 15133 = 48125, birch 73966 - 31174 = 42792, cobalt 32516 + 14445 = 46961. The batch is finished.
